bank.explanation: Class 5.2 (Organic Peroxides) can be unstable and are prone to exothermic decomposition if they are not stored or handled correctly.
The 'overpack' mark must be clearly visible and the word 'OVERPACK' must be in the official language of the country of origin and also in English, French, or German.
bank.question: If an overpack is used, and markings on the internal packages are not visible, the word 'OVERPACK' must be marked on the outside.
A driver may open a package of dangerous goods to check its condition if they suspect it is leaking.
bank.explanation: ADR regulations prohibit any person from opening a package containing dangerous goods during transit.
While Class 9 labels usually indicate general hazards, some goods like asbestos or lithium batteries pose specific risks that require this classification.
bank.question: Class 9 substances are categorized as miscellaneous dangerous goods that do not fit into other hazard classes.
The 'Small Load' exemption points limit is determined based on the Gross Vehicle Weight (GVW) of the van or lorry.
bank.explanation: The 1000-point threshold (1.1.3.6 exemption) relates to the quantity of dangerous goods on the vehicle, not the gross weight of the vehicle itself.

bank.question: When a vehicle has been fully unloaded of all dangerous goods and cleaned, the orange-coloured plates must be removed or covered.
bank.explanation: The orange plates must be removed or covered when the vehicle is no longer carrying dangerous goods (or the residues of those goods).
The portable lighting apparatus (torch) must not have any metallic surface capable of producing a spark.
bank.question: A standard metal-cased flashlight is acceptable for use during the transport of flammable gases as long as the batteries are new.
Eye protection, such as safety goggles, is part of the mandatory personal protective equipment for every member of the vehicle crew.
bank.explanation: ADR requires that every member of the vehicle crew is provided with an eye protection (e.g., protective goggles).
A Packing Group I (high danger) container is more robustly tested than a Packing Group III (low danger) container.
bank.question: A container tested to Packing Group III standards is also legally authorized to carry substances assigned to Packing Group I.
A driver transporting goods under the 1.1.3.6 'Small Load' exemption must still receive appropriate awareness training.
bank.explanation: Under ADR, even if a driver is working under the Small Load exemption (1.1.3.6), they must attend 'awareness training' to understand the hazards and emergency procedures.
The Instructions in Writing (Emergency Instructions) must be provided in a language that the vehicle crew can read and understand.
bank.question: Instructions in Writing must always be provided in French, regardless of the driver's native language.

bank.explanation: Substances in Packing Group I are categorized as high danger, Group II as medium danger, and Group III as low danger.
bank.question: Packing Group I substances represent the highest level of danger within a specific hazard class.
For certain classes of dangerous goods, the vehicle must carry a drain seal to prevent environmental contamination in the event of a leak.
bank.explanation: A drain seal is a mandatory piece of equipment for certain classes (3, 4.1, 4.3, 8, and 9) to prevent spilled chemicals from entering the sewage system.

bank.question: The 1.1.3.6 threshold (Small Load exemption) can be used when transporting dangerous goods in a road tanker.
bank.explanation: The 'Small Load' exemption (1.1.3.6) only applies to packages (e.g., drums, boxes, pallets) and does not apply to goods carried in tanks or in bulk.
The orange-coloured plates must be removed or covered when the vehicle is no longer carrying dangerous goods and has been cleaned.
bank.question: Orange-coloured plates should remain displayed on a vehicle even after all packages have been unloaded and the vehicle is empty.

bank.explanation: Intermediate Bulk Containers (IBCs) are larger than standard drums but are still classified and regulated under the ADR 'Packages' rules.
bank.question: An IBC (Intermediate Bulk Container) is considered a package under the ADR regulations.
Water is the recommended extinguishing agent for all fires involving Class 4.3 (Dangerous when wet) substances.
bank.explanation: Class 4.3 substances react with water to emit flammable gases, so using water to extinguish a fire involving these could be extremely dangerous.
UN numbers are standard four-digit codes used globally to identify specific hazardous substances or groups of substances.
bank.question: Every separate item of dangerous goods must be assigned a four-digit UN number.

bank.explanation: The driver is responsible for checking that the load is properly secured and that the vehicle is correctly marked before starting the journey.
bank.question: The driver has no responsibility for ensuring the load is secure; this is the sole legal responsibility of the warehouse loader.
The 'Environmentally Hazardous Substance' mark is required for packages containing goods that pose a risk to the aquatic environment.
bank.explanation: Substances that are hazardous to the environment (UN 3077 and UN 3082) require the 'dead fish and tree' mark on the packaging.
Smoking and the use of electronic cigarettes are strictly prohibited on or near the vehicle during the loading, unloading, and carriage of dangerous goods.
bank.question: Smoking is permitted inside the vehicle cab during the transport of dangerous goods as long as the windows are closed.
A flashlight used on a vehicle carrying flammable goods must not have any metallic surfaces capable of producing sparks.
bank.explanation: ADR prohibits portable lighting with exposed metal surfaces that could produce sparks; lights must be designed to avoid igniting flammable vapours.
While some mixing is allowed, the ADR segregation table prohibits certain goods, like Class 1 (Explosives) and Class 5.1 (Oxidisers), from being loaded together.
bank.question: Any two different hazard classes can always be loaded onto the same vehicle if they are both in packages.

bank.explanation: The driver must ensure the vehicle is not overloaded and is legally responsible for the safe transport and compliance of the load once on the road.
bank.question: Under ADR, the driver is legally responsible for ensuring the total quantity of dangerous goods on the vehicle does not exceed the allowed limits.
Under the 1.1.3.6 (Small Load) exemption, the vehicle is not required to carry any fire extinguishers.
bank.explanation: While they do not need full ADR orange plates, vehicles under the 1.1.3.6 exemption must carry at least one 2kg dry powder fire extinguisher.
A written declaration from the consignor is required to provide emergency responders and the carrier with precise information about the hazards.
bank.question: Every consignment of dangerous goods must be accompanied by a transport document (load hazard sheet) provided by the consignor.
The 'Instructions in Writing' must be provided in the native language of the country of origin, regardless of what the driver speaks.
bank.explanation: The Instruction in Writing (Emergency Instructions) must be provided in a language that the vehicle crew can read and understand.
Substances assigned to Packing Group II are defined as 'medium danger' materials within their hazard class.
bank.question: Packing Group II signifies that the substance being transported is of medium danger.
Dangerous goods belonging to Class 7 are categorized as Organic Peroxides.
bank.explanation: Class 7 covers radioactive materials; organic peroxides are classified under Class 5.2.
Under ADR, 'Packages' refers to the complete product of the packing operation, which includes the packaging itself and its contents.
bank.question: The term 'Package' in ADR specifically refers to the combination of the packaging and the dangerous goods contained within it.

bank.explanation: Subsidery risk labels are just as important as primary labels and must be displayed on the package if the contents have multiple hazards.
bank.question: If a package has a subsidiary risk label, it can be smaller or less visible than the primary hazard label.

bank.explanation: The wheel chock must be sized appropriately for the maximum mass of the vehicle and the diameter of the wheels to ensure it effectively prevents movement.
bank.question: Every vehicle transporting dangerous goods that requires orange plates must carry at least one wheel chock of a size suited to the vehicle's weight.

bank.explanation: Small Load limits vary (e.g., 20, 333, or 1000) based on the Transport Category of the specific goods, not a flat 500kg for all items.
bank.question: The transport category threshold for the 'Small Load' exemption is always 500 units for every type of dangerous good.

bank.explanation: Under ADR, the driver is restricted from opening any package containing dangerous goods to ensure safety and prevent exposure or spills.
bank.question: A driver is strictly prohibited from opening a package containing dangerous goods unless authorised by the carrier.

bank.explanation: Small vehicles under 3.5 tonnes are still required to carry a minimum of one 2kg dry powder extinguisher if they are carrying dangerous goods above the 1.1.3.6 threshold.
bank.question: Vehicles with a maximum permissible mass of less than 3.5 tonnes carrying packages are exempt from carrying any fire extinguishers.

bank.explanation: Class 5.2 (Organic Peroxides) substances are unstable and often require strict temperature control to prevent decomposition or explosion.
bank.question: Some substances within Class 5.2 (Organic Peroxides) may require temperature control during transport as specified in the ADR regulations.

bank.explanation: A Mixed Loading prohibited table exists; for example, Class 1 (Explosives) generally cannot be loaded with other hazard classes on the same vehicle.
bank.question: Dangerous goods of Class 1 (Explosive substances) can be loaded into the same vehicle as Class 5.1 (Oxidising substances) without restriction.

bank.explanation: Overpacks must be marked with the word 'OVERPACK' and show the UN numbers and hazard labels of the packages inside unless they are clearly visible.
bank.question: When using an overpack, the word 'OVERPACK' must be clearly marked on the outside if the internal labels are not visible.

bank.explanation: Packing Group I represents the highest level of danger, while Packing Group III represents the lowest danger level.
bank.question: Packing Group III indicates a substance that poses a high level of danger to the environment and the public.
